_tool_scope: This file is an evaluation definition — it is not executed as agent instructions. Assertions of type 'llm_judge' are grading metadata, not tool grants. The skill itself uses read/write file access and orchestrates sub-agents; it does not grant blanket tool access.

evals.prompt: Necesito documentar mi proyecto de backend en Node.js, no tengo ningún doc todavía
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator should: (1) detect missing domain/audience context and ask clarifying questions, OR if sufficient context exists, proceed to delegate to doc-auditor with docs_path='none — new project'. It should present a status matrix showing all 7 documents with action=CREAR and propose the documentation plan.

assertions.text: The response invokes or delegates to the doc-auditor agent with a properly formatted AUDITOR INPUT block

The response presents or describes a status matrix with all 7 required documents (index.md, project-overview.md, requirements.md, project-structure.md, tech-stack.md, features.md, implementation.md, user-flow.md)
The response does NOT attempt to generate any document content — it only audits and proposes a plan

evals.prompt: Help me write the technical docs for my React dashboard project, I already have a README
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator should detect an existing doc (README), ask for or infer the docs/ path, then delegate to doc-auditor. The auditor should classify README as an existing file and flag it for possible mapping to project-overview.md or index.md. The response should present a status matrix distinguishing existing vs missing documents and offer to audit + complete.

assertions.text: The response acknowledges the existing README and incorporates it into the audit plan rather than ignoring it
The response delegates to doc-auditor (not directly to doc-generator) and shows a delegation input block
The response uses English throughout, matching the input language

evals.prompt: Audit my docs/ folder at src/docs and tell me what's missing
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator should invoke doc-auditor ONLY with docs_path='src/docs'. It should NOT proceed to the Interviewer or Generator. The response is a status matrix showing which of the 7 documents exist, their content state, and required actions.

assertions.text: The response invokes doc-auditor with docs_path set to 'src/docs'
The response does NOT invoke doc-interviewer or doc-generator — the workflow stops after the audit
The response presents a status matrix table listing each of the 7 required documents with their status

evals.prompt: Write only the requirements.md for my Flutter mobile app
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator should skip the full audit phase (or run a minimal one) and directly invoke doc-interviewer for requirements.md only, then hand off to doc-generator. The interviewer should ask Flutter-domain-specific questions about functional requirements, technical requirements, quality requirements, and environments.

assertions.text: The response invokes doc-interviewer with doc_name='requirements.md' and domain='mobile' or detected_stack containing 'Flutter'
The response does NOT generate all 7 documents — it scopes the workflow to requirements.md only
The interviewer questions are adapted to Flutter/mobile context (e.g., mentions pubspec, widgets, platforms, or app stores)

evals.prompt: ¿Cuáles son las mejores prácticas para documentar APIs REST?
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator should recognize this as a general knowledge question, NOT a project documentation request. It should answer briefly with REST API documentation best practices (OpenAPI/Swagger, versioning, endpoint descriptions, error codes, examples) without triggering the 4-agent orchestration workflow.

assertions.text: The response does NOT invoke doc-auditor, doc-interviewer, doc-generator, or doc-validator
The response answers in Spanish, matching the input language
The response mentions at least one concrete REST API documentation tool or standard (e.g., OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, or similar)
